speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, could you describe any new or worsening involuntary movements, such as muscle rigidity or tremors, alongside the fever? Also, have you noticed any dark urine or yellowing of your eyes recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS).

The combination of fever, altered mental status, generalized rigidity, profuse sweating, and recent haloperidol use is highly suggestive of NMS. While your reflexes are currently normal, this condition can progress rapidly to life-threatening instability. I recommend immediate admission for supportive care, discontinuation of haloperidol, and initiation of dantrolene or bromocriptine.
